channel.title: Increvio Guides
channel.description: Research-backed guides on staying consistent, nutrition and training.

item.title: How to Stay Consistent With Working Out (When Motivation Fades)
item.description: Motivation fades, systems don't. 9 research-backed ways to stay consistent with working out: plans, habits, friends, smaller wins and never missing twice.

item.title: How Long Does It Take to Form a Habit? (Not 21 Days)
item.description: The 21-day rule is a myth. Research says habits take 66 days on average, with a range of 18 to 254. Here's what that means for your workouts and diet.

item.title: How to Get Motivated to Work Out (and What to Do When You're Not)
item.description: No motivation to work out? 10 research-backed ways to get yourself to the gym, plus why waiting for motivation is the wrong strategy in the first place.

item.title: Never Miss Twice: The Simple Rule That Saves Your Progress
item.description: Missing one workout doesn't hurt your progress. Missing two in a row starts a new habit. How the never-miss-twice rule works and how to use it.

item.title: Accountability Partner for Fitness: Why It Works and How to Find One
item.description: People who started with friends were far more likely to finish their program. How a fitness accountability partner works, who to pick, and how to set it up.

item.title: Why People Quit Working Out: 7 Reasons and How to Avoid Them
item.description: Most people who start working out quit within weeks. The 7 most common reasons, from all-or-nothing plans to invisible progress, and how to avoid each one.

item.title: When-Then Plans: The Easiest Way to Actually Do Your Workouts
item.description: Writing down when and where you'll exercise raised follow-through to 91% in one study. How to make when-then plans for training and food.

item.title: How to Get Back on Track After Falling Off Your Fitness Routine
item.description: Fell off your workout or diet routine? How to restart without guilt, how much strength you actually lost, and a simple 2-week plan to get back on track.

item.title: Do Fitness Streaks Work? How to Use Streaks Without Burning Out
item.description: Streaks can make habits stick, but a broken streak can make people quit. What research says about streaks and how to design one that keeps you going.

item.title: How to Make Working Out a Habit: A Step-by-Step System
item.description: Turn exercise into a habit you don't have to think about. A step-by-step system built on habit research: cues, tiny starts, rewards and repetition.

item.title: Gym Anxiety: How to Feel Confident at the Gym as a Beginner
item.description: Nervous about going to the gym? Gym anxiety is common and fixable. 10 practical steps to feel confident, from a written plan to quiet times and small exposures.

item.title: Morning vs Evening Workout: Which Is Better?
item.description: Is it better to work out in the morning or evening? What research says about time of day for strength, muscle and fat loss, and which time helps you stay consistent.

item.title: How to Stay Motivated to Lose Weight (When Progress Slows)
item.description: Losing motivation to lose weight? What people who keep weight off actually do, why progress feels slow, and 9 research-backed ways to keep going.

item.title: How to Build Discipline for Fitness (Without Relying on Willpower)
item.description: Discipline isn't about forcing yourself. Research shows disciplined people rely on habits and fewer temptations. How to build discipline for training and eating.

item.title: All-or-Nothing Mindset: Why It Ruins Your Fitness and How to Stop
item.description: Missed one workout, so the week is ruined? The all-or-nothing mindset is the #1 reason diets and training plans collapse. How to replace it with something that works.

item.title: How to Track Fitness Progress (Beyond the Scale)
item.description: The scale alone is a bad progress tracker. How to track fitness progress with weight trends, measurements, strength, photos and consistency, and how often to check.

item.title: How to Work Out With a Busy Schedule (and Actually Stick to It)
item.description: No time to work out? How busy people fit training into a full schedule: minimum effective dose, short sessions, exercise snacks and planning that survives chaos.

item.title: How to Stick to a Diet: 10 Strategies That Actually Work
item.description: The best diet is the one you can stick to. 10 research-backed strategies to stay on track with healthy eating, from meal planning to the 80/20 rule.

item.title: How Much Protein Per Day? The Research-Backed Answer
item.description: How much protein do you need per day to build muscle or lose fat? Research says 1.6 to 2.2 g per kg. Tables by body weight, timing and food examples.

item.title: How Many Calories to Build Muscle? Lean Bulk Without Getting Fat
item.description: You need a small calorie surplus to build muscle, not a big one. How to calculate your calories, how fast to gain, and why a lean bulk beats dirty bulking.

item.title: How Fast Should You Lose Weight? A Safe, Realistic Pace
item.description: Aim to lose about 0.5 to 1% of your body weight per week. Why slower fat loss protects muscle, how to set your deficit, and what to expect month by month.

item.title: Meal Prep for Beginners: A Simple Sunday System
item.description: Meal prep for beginners, step by step. How to plan, shop and cook a week of healthy meals in about 2 hours, with a sample plan, storage times and tips.

item.title: How to Make a Weekly Meal Plan and Grocery List (Template)
item.description: How to build a healthy weekly meal plan and a grocery list sorted by aisle in 20 minutes. Step-by-step method, example week and tips to save time and money.

item.title: Eating Out on a Diet: How to Enjoy Restaurants Without Losing Progress
item.description: You don't have to skip restaurants to lose fat or build muscle. What to order when eating out on a diet and how to adjust your day.

item.title: Weight Loss Plateau: Why It Happens and How to Break It
item.description: Stuck on a weight loss plateau? Why progress slows down, how to tell a real plateau from water weight, and 6 research-backed ways to get moving again.

item.title: Creatine: What It Does, How Much to Take and Is It Safe?
item.description: The most researched supplement for strength and muscle. What creatine does, how much to take (3 to 5 g a day), timing and safety.

item.title: How to Lose Weight Without Feeling Hungry All the Time
item.description: Hunger is the main reason diets fail. 9 research-backed ways to stay full in a calorie deficit, from protein and volume foods to sleep and a moderate pace.

item.title: High-Protein Snacks: 25 Easy Ideas With 15 to 30 g Protein
item.description: Easy high-protein snacks for muscle gain and fat loss, with protein per serving. Sweet, savory, no-prep and on-the-go ideas, plus how to fit them into your day.

item.title: How Much Water Should You Drink a Day? (Including Workouts)
item.description: How much water you need per day, including food and training. Official guidelines (2 to 2.5 L total), signs of good hydration and how to drink more without thinking.

item.title: Calorie Deficit Explained: How to Calculate Yours
item.description: What a calorie deficit is, how to calculate your maintenance calories and a safe deficit, why the 3,500 kcal rule is too simple, and how to adjust as you go.

item.title: Macros Explained: How to Set Protein, Carbs and Fat
item.description: What macros are and how to set them for muscle gain or fat loss. Protein first (1.6 to 2.2 g/kg), fat 20 to 35% of calories, carbs fill the rest. Examples included.

item.title: Healthy Eating on a Budget: High-Protein Meals That Don't Cost Much
item.description: How to eat healthy and high-protein on a budget. The cheapest protein sources, a sample grocery list, meal prep tips and why frozen vegetables are a smart buy.

item.title: What to Eat Before and After a Workout (Simple Guide)
item.description: What to eat before and after training for muscle gain and performance. Timing, protein and carbs, the truth about the "anabolic window", and easy meal ideas.

item.title: Alcohol and Fitness: How Drinking Affects Muscle and Fat Loss
item.description: How alcohol affects muscle building, fat loss, sleep and recovery, and how to drink smarter if you want to keep your progress. Honest, research-based.

item.title: Does Intermittent Fasting Work? What the Research Says
item.description: Does intermittent fasting help you lose more fat? Large trials show 16:8 works about as well as normal calorie restriction. Who it suits, and how to do it with training.

item.title: How to Start Working Out: A Beginner's Guide That Sticks
item.description: New to working out? How to start strength training as a beginner: how often, which exercises, how heavy, a simple 3-day plan, and how to make it stick.

item.title: How Many Sets Per Week to Build Muscle? The Research Answer
item.description: Aim for at least 10 hard sets per muscle per week to build muscle. What the research says about training volume, how to count sets and how to split them.

item.title: Progressive Overload Explained: How to Keep Getting Stronger
item.description: Progressive overload is how you keep building muscle and strength. What it is, why it works, and the double progression method that makes it simple.

item.title: How Many Days a Week Should You Work Out?
item.description: How many days a week should you work out to build muscle or lose fat? Research-backed answers for 2, 3, 4 and 5 days, with example splits for each.

item.title: No Time to Work Out? How to Train Effectively in 20 to 30 Minutes
item.description: No time for the gym? How to build muscle and stay consistent with short 20 to 30 minute workouts, using supersets, smart exercise choice and fewer warm-up sets.

item.title: How Close to Failure Should You Train to Build Muscle?
item.description: Do you need to train to failure to build muscle? Research says stopping 1 to 2 reps short works about as well, with less fatigue. How to judge reps in reserve.

item.title: Cardio or Weights for Fat Loss? Why You Need Both
item.description: Cardio or weights for fat loss? Diet drives fat loss, weights protect muscle, cardio adds burn. How to combine them without losing gains.

item.title: Muscle Soreness (DOMS): Should You Train When You're Sore?
item.description: Why muscles get sore 1 to 3 days after training, whether soreness means growth, what actually helps, and when you can (and can't) train through it.

item.title: Full Body vs Split Workout: Which Is Better for You?
item.description: Full body or split routine? When weekly volume is equal, both build similar muscle. How to choose based on your schedule, plus example full body, upper/lower and PPL weeks.

item.title: Home Workout Without Equipment: Build Muscle With Bodyweight
item.description: Can you build muscle at home without equipment? Yes, if sets are hard and you progress. A full bodyweight plan, how to make exercises harder, and what to buy first.

item.title: How Much Rest Between Sets to Build Muscle?
item.description: How long to rest between sets for muscle and strength. Longer rest (2 to 3 min) on big lifts helps you lift more; shorter rest works for small exercises and supersets.

item.title: Deload Week: What It Is and When You Need One
item.description: A deload is a planned lighter week to manage fatigue. When to take one, how to do it (half the sets, easier effort), and what research says about losing gains.

item.title: How Many Steps a Day Do You Really Need?
item.description: Do you need 10,000 steps a day? Large studies show benefits level off around 6,000 to 8,000 for older adults and 8,000 to 10,000 for younger adults. How steps help fat loss.

item.title: Sleep and Muscle Growth: Why 7+ Hours Matter for Your Gains
item.description: How sleep affects muscle building, fat loss, hunger and training. What research shows about short sleep, how much you need, and 8 tips to sleep better as an athlete.

item.title: How to Warm Up Before Lifting Weights (5-Minute Routine)
item.description: A simple, effective warm-up for strength training: a few minutes of light cardio, dynamic movements and ramp-up sets. What to skip, and why long static stretching isn't needed.

item.title: The Best App to Stay Consistent With Working Out: What to Look For
item.description: Most people quit their fitness app within weeks. 7 features that actually help you stay consistent, based on behavior research, and how to pick the right app.

item.title: Meal Plan App With Grocery List: What to Look For
item.description: What makes a good meal planning app with a grocery list for fitness goals: protein targets, your taste and budget, aisle-sorted lists, prep guides and replanning.

item.title: Workout App With Friends: How Social Fitness Apps Keep You Going
item.description: Training with friends keeps people consistent. What to look for in a workout app with friends: check-ins, nudges, shared streaks, weekly competition and privacy.

item.title: Fitness App for Beginners: What to Look For Before You Start
item.description: Starting out? What a good beginner fitness app should do: start at your level, explain exercises, plan simple workouts, keep you accountable and set realistic goals.

item.title: Habit Tracker vs Fitness Coach App: Which Helps You Stick With It?
item.description: Should you use a habit tracker or a fitness coach app? A habit tracker shows consistency; a coach app also plans workouts and meals. Pros, cons and who each suits.
